morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Masculine a-stem nouns are Wright's masculine a-stems. Kept distinct from neuter a-stems because gender changes the paradigm.
Neuter a-stem nouns are Wright's neuter a-stems. Kept distinct from masculine a-stems because neuter nominative/accusative behavior differs.
Wright treats masculine ja-stems separately from pure a-stems; the distinction is useful because historical j can affect stem shape.
Wright treats neuter ja-stems separately; kept distinct from masculine ja-stems because gender affects the paradigm.
Wright treats masculine wa-stems separately; historical w can affect forms.
Wright treats neuter wa-stems separately; kept distinct from masculine wa-stems because gender affects the paradigm.
Wright writes o-stem; the normalized modern label is ō-stem. Collapsed because they name the same class.
Wright writes jo-stem; the normalized modern label is jō-stem. Collapsed because they name the same class.
Wright writes wo-stem; the normalized modern label is wō-stem. Collapsed because they name the same class.
Wright separates feminine abstract nouns in -i from the ordinary feminine ō/jō/wō classes.
Kept distinct because gender and historical i-stem membership affect mapping and sometimes forms.
Kept distinct because feminine i-stems map to their own Wright sections.
Kept distinct because neuter i-stems map to their own Wright sections.
Wright treats masculine u-stems separately; sunu is the paradigmatic noun.
Wright treats feminine u-stems separately; duru is the paradigmatic noun.
Wright treats neuter u-stems as remnants. Kept as a class because it has a distinct Wright section.
Collapsed n-stem, weak, and an-declension because they refer to the same practical class; gender remains distinct.
Collapsed n-stem, weak, and an-declension because they refer to the same practical class; gender remains distinct.
Collapsed n-stem, weak, and an-declension because they refer to the same practical class; gender remains distinct.
Collapsed root-noun and monosyllabic consonant-stem; gender is retained because Wright splits the paradigms.
Collapsed root-noun and monosyllabic consonant-stem; gender is retained because Wright splits the paradigms.
Collapsed root-noun and monosyllabic consonant-stem; neuter is retained because Wright gives a distinct remnant section.
Wright §414 includes þ-stems. Kept by gender because dictionary gender can distinguish use, even though Wright uses one section.
Wright §414 includes þ-stems. Kept by gender because dictionary gender can distinguish use, even though Wright uses one section.
Wright §414 includes þ-stems. Kept by gender because dictionary gender can distinguish use, even though Wright uses one section.
Collapsed r-stem, kinship-noun, and family-noun. Kept by gender because dictionary gender distinguishes masculine and feminine kinship nouns.
Collapsed r-stem, kinship-noun, and family-noun. Kept by gender because dictionary gender distinguishes masculine and feminine kinship nouns.
morph_classes.notes: mōþor is treated as a spelling variant of mōdor for class purposes.

morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Collapsed nd-stem and present-participle noun because they refer to the same practical Wright class.
Collapsed s-stem, z-stem, os-es stem, and r-plural because they name the same practical Old English class.
Modern anomalous/irregular label maps to Wright's treatment of the substantive verb under verbs in -mi.
dōn has its own Wright section and is not safely generated from a regular weak or strong class.
gān has its own Wright section and is not safely generated from a regular weak or strong class.
willan has its own Wright section; nyllan is best treated with it as the negative counterpart.
Kept as Wright's preterite-present class I because the class is distinguishable by lexeme/principal parts.
Kept as Wright's preterite-present class II because the class is distinguishable by lexeme/principal parts.
Kept as Wright's preterite-present class III because the class is distinguishable by lexeme/principal parts.
Kept as Wright's preterite-present class IV because the class is distinguishable by lexeme/principal parts.
magan is the practical paradigmatic preterite-present verb and maps to Wright's class V.
Kept as Wright's preterite-present class VI because the class is distinguishable by lexeme/principal parts.
Kept as Wright's preterite-present class VII because the class is distinguishable by lexeme/principal parts.

morph_classes.wright_label: weak verbs, class I, short stems
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Wright distinguishes weak I verbs with originally short stem-syllables; this is programmatically useful from stem shape and principal forms.

morph_classes.wright_label: weak verbs, class I, geminated short-stem type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept distinct because gemination is visible in the headword/stem and affects generation.

morph_classes.wright_label: weak verbs, class I, settan type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept distinct because Wright gives settan-type verbs separately and stem behavior can be recognized from headword/stem.

morph_classes.wright_label: weak verbs, class I, long stems and polysyllabic verbs
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept distinct because long/polysyllabic weak I verbs are programmatically distinguishable from headword/stem shape.

morph_classes.wright_label: weak verbs, class I, irregular or special types
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept as a practical bucket because these verbs require lexeme-level handling and Wright gives them separate sections.
Weak II regular -ian/-ode verbs are programmatically recognizable from headword and principal forms.

morph_classes.canonical_name: weak class 2 contracted or class-III-origin type
morph_classes.wright_label: weak verbs, class II, special contracted/class III origin verbs
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept distinct because Wright gives a separate section and these verbs require special handling.
Weak III is small enough to model lexeme-by-lexeme.
Default strong class I pattern.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class I, fricative alternation
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because alternation is visible in principal parts and affects generation.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class I, contracted tēon-type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because contracted verbs require special handling and Wright gives a separate section.
Default strong class II ēo-type pattern.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class II, s/r alternation
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because s/r alternation is visible from principal parts and affects generated forms.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class II, contracted type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because contracted class II verbs require special handling.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class III, nasal + consonant
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because the post-vocalic consonant environment is programmatically distinguishable.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class III, liquid + consonant
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because the post-vocalic consonant environment is programmatically distinguishable.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class III, breaking type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because the broken vowels and cluster environment are programmatically distinguishable.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class III, feolan type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because Wright gives a separate section and it is not a broad headword-derived class.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class III, miscellaneous special verbs
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept as a lexeme-specific bucket because Wright gives a separate section and forms require special handling.

morph_classes.canonical_name: strong class 4 liquid or nasal type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Default strong class IV type.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class IV, cuman/niman type
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because Wright gives a separate section and these common verbs require special handling.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class V, contracted type

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class VI, contracted slēan-type

Kept because j-present/mutated strong VI verbs are distinguishable and affect generation.

morph_classes.wright_label: strong verbs, class VII, preterite ē subdivision
morph_classes.mapping_rationale: Kept because Wright divides class VII by preterite vowel and this is visible in principal parts.
